title: Candid Rooms — Apartamento Home Tour Opener
description: A full-bleed candid interior photograph carries the entire canvas while all type pools quietly at the lower quarter: an italic serif caption, a bullet-separated issue-and-city tag in 9pt small caps, and the homeowner's name as a near-invisible typographic inset. Nothing here is staged for the camera.
philosophy: This template is built on editorial restraint — the photograph is the argument, and the layout's only job is to stay out of its way. It rejects hero typography, centered hierarchy, and any graphic gesture that signals 'presentation' rather than 'document'. It is for editors, curators, and storytellers who believe one honest image outweighs ten clever slides, and for audiences willing to sit with a room before moving on.
goodFor: Home-tour editorial openers anchored by a single dominant interior photograph
3-line italic serif captions tucked beneath a candid, unstaged room shot
Issue-and-city provenance tags in an Apartamento or Kinfolk editorial register
Slow, contemplative decks for design, interiors, or lifestyle audiences
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews where data must occupy the upper canvas
Multi-image grid layouts that compete with the full-bleed photograph
Rapid-fire pitch decks requiring dense bullet lists above the fold
Dark-background presentations where the warm cream caption box loses contrast
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a page pulled from a slow-print magazine left open on a side table — unhurried, ambient, slightly unguarded, as though the photographer arrived mid-afternoon and shot without rearranging a single object. Text sits as a quiet, gravity-pulled tenant in the lower register, never asserting itself over the image above. The compositional rhythm is asymmetric and bottom-weighted, with the upper three-quarters given entirely over to the room. Avoid any gesture that reads as 'designed': no vignettes, no geometric overlays, no centered staging, nothing that signals a presentation rather than a document.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed photograph bleeds to all four canvas edges with zero margin — the image is the entire slide. Type is confined to the lower 22–25% of the canvas, left-aligned with a 6–8% inset from the left edge. Hierarchy reads top-to-bottom within that lower band: italic serif title line first, then a small-caps issue-and-city provenance tag below it separated by a mid-dot bullet, then the homeowner name as a near-invisible typographic whisper beneath. No header band, no page number, no decorative rule of any kind — the photograph's own edge is the only framing device.

examples.promptCore: The slide should read like a single spread held open inside a slow, object-attentive interiors quarterly — image as primary argument, all language as quiet footnote. Composition is gravity-fed and asymmetric: visual and textual weight pools at the bottom quarter while the photograph occupies the upper canvas unchallenged and unframed. The mood is candid and slightly underdressed, as though the room was caught mid-afternoon with no preparation. Avoid any overlay, decorative border, or typographic gesture that signals deliberate slideware design rather than editorial documentary restraint.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with the photograph bleeding to all four edges, no inset or frame. A text band in the lower 22–25% of the canvas holds three stacked elements inside cols 2–9: an extended italic serif caption of two to three lines, a small-caps room-name or homeowner attribution set at reduced size directly beneath it, and a bullet-separated provenance tag flush-left below that. Folio number sits bottom-right, outside the column grid and the text band entirely. No header, no decorative rule above the text band — the photograph's visual horizon is the only structural divider.
